beats.say: In 1863, a secret Union cavalry unit called the Jessie Scouts infiltrated Confederate lines to gather intel.
They disguised themselves as Southern farmers, slipping through night markets near Vicksburg with forged passes.
Their biggest prize: a hidden cache of Confederate telegram codes discovered behind a church attic in Jackson.
Using these codes, Union General Grant intercepted a plan to reinforce Pickett's Charge before Gettysburg.
The intercepted message forced the Union to reposition artillery, turning the tide at Cemetery Ridge.
Confederates never realized their secret codes were compromised, believing their victory was assured.
The success sparked a Union crackdown on Confederate espionage, leading to the capture of several spies.
Meanwhile, the Union navy's ironclad USS Monitor silently patrolled the James River, intimidating Richmond.
These covert actions kept the Union one step ahead, shaping the war's final chapters.
So remember, the hidden spy war of 1863 was as fierce as any battlefield you see.
